newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee off high after hitting 15-1/2 mth peak.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee off high after hitting 15-1/2 mth peak.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures, powered by fund-led buying and driven by surging New York, rocketed to 15-1/2-month peak basis July on Friday morning trade.
Traders also noted a small degree of roaster price-fixing as the market crossed the pyschologically-important $2,000 barrier for the first time since April 1996.
Benchmark July gathered more steam to hit an intraday high of $2,060 a tonne, a level not seen since January 31, 1996 as the market triggered a few buy-stops on the way up.

But a mixture of spec profit-taking and origin sales pulled the market back to $2,034 by midsession, still a hefty $101 gain. At its peak this morning, the market had gained by 6.5 percent on the day.
Traders said the funds had been massively long in robustas since the frenzied buying from early January that triggered the current five-month rally.
"The funds are about 18,000-lot longs in robustas," said one European coffee roaster.
Traders noted light origin offers this morning but added producers could return on a large scale if the market continued to climb.
New York was called to open unchanged based on London's performance but traders said the opening calls were now immaterial in view of the sharp volatility in the market.
The arabicas soared to 20-year highs basis May on Thursday in a dizzy rally on frantic buying from speculators and commercial coffee firms worried about low reserves and poor crop prospects.
May coffee was traded as high as 279 cents a lb, the highest since June 1977.
Jitteries over the fast approaching Brazilian frost season could help sustain current rally.
This week's surge in bean prices could trigger fresh retail price hike by roasters in Europe after having to put up prices in March and April.

Roasters warned that if prices stay at these levels, coffee consumption could fall by up to 10 million bags a year on a global basis as consumers turn to other alternatives such as tea and soft drinks.
Market attention will focus on key producer talks in London on Monday and Wednesday to consider future of their current export quota programme beyond June this year.

The U.S. green coffee stock data for April released on Thursday were seen as neutral. The stocks showed a rise of 198,000 bags against market expectations of 100,000 to 300,000 bags. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
